I've had these for 2 months now, it's perfect for my noisy warehouse work environment. Got them for only $50 usd. I needed some new buds for my new Galaxy S25 Ultra. I figured the cheap earbuds wouldn't be bad if they're compatible with THE flagship Samsung phone.

And so far. It's phonemenal. I never had ANC earbuds before and this pair really sold me on it. Now I do work 10 hour shifts and these buds usually die after 4-5 hours with ANC at 70-80% volume. But the case charges them enough to basically last through the day. Just 30 minutes of downtime during lunch and these charge back up to 80% quick. 

On my off days, I bring these to workout outside and the call quality isn't actually bad. NTM, my phone also has voice amplification for myself. They don't fall out during my exercises and I can sleep with them on and not feel uncomfortable.

The sound quality will always be subjective. So with the EQ settings. You can make it so that voice clarity is much more audible even in the most heavy instrumental music. Or bass boosted for those amazing lows. I set mine to Dynamic and it has been the best buds for me to date.

8/10 for the sound quality
7/10 for battery 
8/10 for aesthetic  and comfort 
9/10 for price
7/10 for daily business

text_raw:
IDK why I absolutely hate these compared to nearly everything else.  Did everything right, but bass is weak, fit is just bad. Smiling or talking will dislodge them, yet they're glossy and so round it's hard to grab to remove when you DO want to take them out. They don't auto-pause when removing one bud (and no way to change that), and then any kind of readjusting almost always triggers some touch function.  Tap to pause, then try to remove one bud, it will inadvertently trigger playing again. This leads you to have to tap the bud that's still in to pause again (as the one you removed no longer responds to touch), requiring two hands just to do this simple thing... And the app doesn't do much to improve things, except let you customize touch functions. 

The only positive feedback I can give is that ANC is actually REALLY good. 

I've really preferred the Jabra Elite 75t; they are leagues better, in almost every way.

author: @brettmiller3688
text_raw:
My wife got the Galaxy Buds 2 (at $149) to go with her Galaxy S21+ phone -- they sounded great.

However, I opted for the Cambridge Audio Melomania 1+ (at $99) to go with my Galaxy S21+ phone -- and they sounded even better! Yes, it has buttons (quelle horreur!) -- but with that "three-out-of-ten" error rate you mentioned (quite true) with the Galaxy Buds 2 touch controls, buttons, all of a sudden, seem less of a negative. Although the Melomania 1+ has no ANC, the optional memory foam eartips do make a good seal, rendering the Samsung's noise cancellation feature kind of "meh."

Not to mention that, even with the Galaxy S21+'s native earbud-phone interface, the downloadable Cambridge Audio Melomania app offers much more control over soundscape preferences, including an actual EQ capability.

Did like the Samsung phone-based fit adjustment feedback idea and the Galaxy Buds 2's transparency mode function, though.

text_raw:
Fit, terrible.

Support, terrible.

Sound, great

Coming from Sony XM4s I wish I still had the Sonys still. Buds 2 are such a waste of money for me.

About 4hr-5hr Battery with one dead bud and one around 15%-20% of life left on them. Taking them on and off will pause music but not play again (sonys did this no issue). Tips degraded within months and because of the dumb name 'buds 2 pro', trying to find tips online leads you to apple, pixel and older samsung buds because of key search words.

I dont need the 'looking down warning' as if i simply look down for too long the buds will just fall out of my ear anyway.

The case is too small and no extra space inside so trying out foam tips are near impossible also due to no extra space.

They need wing tips or something more then anything else. I tried sticking foam on the back but because of the case you cant close it. I use double sided tape now and even 0.01mm tape sticks to the case.

ANC is useless 100%. Ambient noise does a weird thing if you touch the buds then they go into ANC but its better then normal ANC somehow!

The mics are trash and after cleaning the mesh as per instructions now the mic is even WORSE on my left bud...enabling ambient noise will make some kind of 'needle touching the record' sound.

Support was useless as they talked and never got back to me. expected me to drive 3 hrs just for new silicone tips!. Ended up getting spinfits but they dont work either.

BT strength is piss poor also, I kneel down and loose connection just with the phone in my pocket too.

My 10+ years of saving old unused tips meant nothing with the buds 2 pro as no older tips worked (even a bunch of comply foams I had) Meaning close to $50 to buy new aftermarket tips because the stock one degraded so fast (never in my life before)

author: @MattisProbably
text_raw:
I bought the Buds3 Pro today. Got them heavily discounted.
And I actually used the Sony XM5s for the last 6 months. But they had pretty severe connection issues, which others report as well... Last Sunday on an electric bus they were basically unusable. The interference from the bus itself made them drop out constantly. At train stations the connection kept dropping out when a train came in.
And today, on my way to pick up the Buds3 Pro, in the downtown area, that wasn't even that crowded, they kept dropping out as I was walking through the crowd.
I tried the mode to prioritize the connection over audio quality, I tried LE audio. Nothing worked. And I had the same issues with the XM3s I used years ago.
So Sony is done for me as far as headphones go.
But I'm very happy with the Buds3 Pro so far. No connection issues, I tuned the EQ and now they basically sound just like the XM5s and the ANC actually seems to be better at blocking train noises. Through higher pitched sounds make it through a bit more.
But yeah, I paid 150 bucks for them, which is the same as the Buds2 Pro here in Germany right now, so I'm happy.

text_raw: Theese are not the AirPods killer, for the same reason as the AirPods themselves. They work well with a Samsung Device only. The lack of aptX and Ldac Bluetooth Codecs, will make these earphones play either with AAC codec (on an iPhone) or AAC and SBC on an Android. The "scalable codec" known as SSC is available on a Galaxy Device only. So in other words : if you have for example a Xiaomi Tablet or Phone (that can run Ldac), and you want to buy the Buds 3, they will sound as any 50-100€ wireless buds. It would be an AirPods killer if Samsung gave the compatibility with other major codecs such as those mentioned above (LDAC from Sony, aptX from Qualcom and L2HC from Huawei). In that case anyone that does not own a samsung device gen enjoy a quality sound. Otherwise you're stuck in their ecosystem in the same way as other people are stuck with the Apple Ecosistem. The reason is that Samsung forces you (in a way) to buy only their products.
